packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — PACKET 01

Isolation: I read this packet's PROMPT.md and its two supplied images only. I have not consulted a catalogue, edition, earlier transcription, web source, repository, or memory, and have not attempted work/author identification. Names below are transcribed citation labels visible in the images, not identifications of the manuscript's work.

Layout survey: Both photographs are upright, with two long columns. Image-001 is very heavily rubbed/faded, especially the right half of its left column and much of the right column; broad brown strips obscure portions of the edges. Image-002 has much clearer black writing and generous blank lower and side margins. Repeated red and blue paragraph signs and red-touched larger initial letters mark entries. No continuous running title is discernible. A small number-like mark appears in the top margin of image-002. There are occasional short oblique marginal strokes and small marginal signs, rather than an extensive separately arranged commentary. I see no systematic interlinear gloss apparatus. Some citation labels and entry text occupy the same physical line. The entries look like a succession of attributed passages; separating a quoted lemma from an independent commentator's prose is not securely possible from layout alone.

Image handling: Original sizes: image-001.jpg 7621 × 11444; image-002.jpg 7706 × 11459. I first inspected complete images reduced to 1700 pixels high for layout only. Transcription was made from native-pixel PNG crops, without resizing, rotation, sharpening, or contrast changes. Coordinates are (left, top, right, bottom), origin upper left:
image-001 i1-left-a (1150,3500,2750,4900); i1-left-b (2600,3500,4200,4900); i1-left-c (1150,6000,2750,7400); i1-left-d (2600,6000,4200,7400).
image-002 i2-left-a (950,1950,2550,3300); i2-left-b (2400,1950,4000,3300); i2-left-c (950,4800,2550,6200); i2-left-d (2400,4800,4000,6200); i2-right-a (4020,2000,5620,3400); i2-right-b (5470,2000,7070,3400).
Paired crops overlap by 150 pixels horizontally; overlap is not additional text.

Numbering: L and R are left and right columns. Numbers count visible physical text lines from the top of that column in the complete image, not from crop tops. Image-001 numbers are provisional because the damaged upper lines are difficult to count. The quoted spans retain physical line breaks. Overbars are retained approximately; parentheses supply proposed expansions. A question mark immediately follows uncertain readings. [illegible] does not imply a known number of missing words.

Coverage and limits: Both complete images were inspected for layout. I examined four separate column regions at native scale: two in image-001 left, two in image-002 left, plus image-002 right. Most of image-001 right and the remaining stretches of both images remain unread. The damaged first image permits fragments but does not support a reliable connecting transcription from the selected regions. The clearer second image gives several entry openings and adjoining prose, but these readings remain provisional, especially the more compressed word groups and abbreviations. No reading has been checked against any external text. I make no source identification.
